key_insight: Zero-shot LLMs improved the trade-off between positive predictive value (PPV) and positive classification yield for interstitial lung disease compared with published claims-based algorithms.
clinical_relevance: More accurate ILD identification could strengthen drug-safety research, including in claims databases without linked clinical notes.
method: Evaluated 12 open-access LLMs using claims, EHR notes, or both, without task-specific training.
Compared performance with 20 published claims-based algorithms using pulmonologist-adjudicated ILD status.
Projected drug-safety effect estimates and sample-size requirements under simulated outcome misclassification.
evidence_signal: Among 309 oncology patients with ILD diagnosis codes, claims-only Qwen3-8B achieved 89.8% PPV at 15.9% yield, versus 86.7% PPV at 4.9% yield for the highest-PPV claims algorithm.
watch_item: Evaluation was limited to code-positive oncology patients at one health system; epidemiological benefits were simulated rather than demonstrated in a drug-safety study.
paper_title: Identifying interstitial lung disease with large language models on clinical notes and claims
